# May All Beings Be Happy

*Snp 1.8, the Metta Sutta — set 2, The Basic Diagnosis and the Path*

<p class="reading-meta"><strong>Reading time:</strong> about 2 min · 267 words</p>

[Skip to the translation](#translation){ .reader-skip-link }

## Before you read

This is one of the most often recited texts in the Buddhist world, usually
called the *Karaṇīya Metta Sutta* after its opening words. It is about
*friendliness*: wishing all beings well, without limit.

It starts with character, not with the wish. Someone who wants to practice
this should be capable, honest, easy to speak to, content, and not greedy.
Only then come the lines most people know: *may all beings be happy at
heart*, whatever and wherever they are.

The central image is a mother protecting her only child with her life. The
text asks you to turn that same care toward all beings, in every direction,
whether you are standing, walking, sitting, or lying down.

The numbers beside the verses count the verses within this discourse.

## Translation

### Verses

<span class="verse-number">1</span><span class="verse-line">This is what should be done by someone skilled in the good,</span>
<span class="verse-line">who has understood the state of peace:</span>
<span class="verse-line">let them be able, upright, truly upright,</span>
<span class="verse-line verse-line--last">easy to speak to, gentle, and not proud,</span>
{: .verse }

<span class="verse-number">2</span><span class="verse-line">content and easy to support,</span>
<span class="verse-line">with few duties and a light way of living,</span>
<span class="verse-line">calm in their senses and alert,</span>
<span class="verse-line verse-line--last">not brash, and not greedy among families.</span>
{: .verse }

<span class="verse-number">3</span><span class="verse-line">Let them not do even the slightest thing</span>
<span class="verse-line">that the wise would criticize them for.</span>
<span class="verse-line">May all be happy and secure;</span>
<span class="verse-line verse-line--last">may all beings be happy at heart.</span>
{: .verse }

<span class="verse-number">4</span><span class="verse-line">Whatever living beings there are,</span>
<span class="verse-line">whether frail or firm, without exception,</span>
<span class="verse-line">long or large,</span>
<span class="verse-line verse-line--last">middling, short, fine, or coarse,</span>
{: .verse }

<span class="verse-number">5</span><span class="verse-line">seen or unseen,</span>
<span class="verse-line">living far away or near,</span>
<span class="verse-line">those who have come to be and those still to come:</span>
<span class="verse-line verse-line--last">may all beings be happy at heart.</span>
{: .verse }

<span class="verse-number">6</span><span class="verse-line">Let no one deceive another</span>
<span class="verse-line">or look down on anyone anywhere.</span>
<span class="verse-line">Let no one, out of anger or resentment,</span>
<span class="verse-line verse-line--last">wish pain on another.</span>
{: .verse }

<span class="verse-number">7</span><span class="verse-line">As a mother would protect with her life</span>
<span class="verse-line">her child, her only child,</span>
<span class="verse-line">so toward all beings</span>
<span class="verse-line verse-line--last">develop a boundless heart.</span>
{: .verse }

<span class="verse-number">8</span><span class="verse-line">Develop a boundless heart</span>
<span class="verse-line">of friendliness toward the whole world,</span>
<span class="verse-line">above, below, and all around,</span>
<span class="verse-line verse-line--last">unobstructed, without hatred, without enmity.</span>
{: .verse }

<span class="verse-number">9</span><span class="verse-line">Standing or walking, sitting</span>
<span class="verse-line">or lying down, as long as you are awake,</span>
<span class="verse-line">resolve on this remembering.</span>
<span class="verse-line verse-line--last">This, they say, is the divine way of living here.</span>
{: .verse }

<span class="verse-number">10</span><span class="verse-line">Not taking up views,</span>
<span class="verse-line">virtuous and accomplished in vision,</span>
<span class="verse-line">with greed for sensuality removed,</span>
<span class="verse-line verse-line--last">they do not come again to lie in a womb.</span>
{: .verse }

The eighth discourse, on friendliness, is finished.

<dt><dfn>friendliness</dfn></dt>
<dd>This project&#x27;s rendering of &quot;mettā&quot; (often translated &quot;loving-kindness&quot;) -- an intentionally cultivated goodwill extended outward, including to people you don&#x27;t know.</dd>
<dt><dfn>greed</dfn></dt>
<dd>One of the three &quot;roots&quot; behind unwholesome action, alongside aversion and delusion -- the acquisitive pull toward what looks satisfying.</dd>
<dt><dfn>heart</dfn></dt>
<dd>This project&#x27;s rendering of &quot;citta&quot; -- the affective or feeling side of mind: the part that takes on a mood, wants, leans, reacts, and can be gladdened, steadied, trained, and released. It is sometimes called the &quot;heart-mind&quot; or &quot;feeling mind&quot;; here &quot;heart&quot; does not mean merely emotion or the physical organ.</dd>
<dt><dfn>remembering</dfn></dt>
<dd>This project&#x27;s rendering of &quot;sati&quot; -- actively keeping what matters in mind and returning to it when it is lost, not bare attention to whatever happens to be present.</dd>
<dt><dfn>world</dfn></dt>
<dd>A word whose scope shifts with the teaching. It can mean the lived world built through the senses and the mind, or the wider physical cosmos. The surrounding passage shows which sense is meant.</dd>

*[friendliness]: This project's rendering of "mettā" (often translated "loving-kindness") -- an intentionally cultivated goodwill extended outward, including to people you don't know.
*[greed]: One of the three "roots" behind unwholesome action, alongside aversion and delusion -- the acquisitive pull toward what looks satisfying.
*[heart]: This project's rendering of "citta" -- the affective or feeling side of mind: the part that takes on a mood, wants, leans, reacts, and can be gladdened, steadied, trained, and released. It is sometimes called the "heart-mind" or "feeling mind"; here "heart" does not mean merely emotion or the physical organ.
*[remembering]: This project's rendering of "sati" -- actively keeping what matters in mind and returning to it when it is lost, not bare attention to whatever happens to be present.
*[world]: A word whose scope shifts with the teaching. It can mean the lived world built through the senses and the mind, or the wider physical cosmos. The surrounding passage shows which sense is meant.
